projects.name: Virtual Garden
projects.tagline: A Chrome extension that grows a garden from your focus.
projects.serious: Time on sites you mark as productive grows a small garden, and the rest makes it wilt. It's built with WXT (Manifest V3), TypeScript and Vitest, with CI on every pull request. It has four themes: zen, cosmic, ocean and pixel.

projects.name: retrieval-tracer
projects.tagline: Retrieval, up close, in the browser.
projects.serious: Sentence embeddings (all-MiniLM-L6-v2) run in the browser through transformers.js, and you can see cosine similarity build up dimension by dimension. Chunking and hybrid search come next.

projects.name: chord-cycle-open
projects.tagline: A chord wheel you play with your hands.
projects.serious: You play it in the browser with a pointer, touch or a webcam. MediaPipe hand tracking picks the chord, opening your hand swells it, and Web Audio plays it. No plugins and no MIDI hardware.
projects.joke: Air guitar, except the chords are correct.

projects.name: desk-3d
projects.serious: A scene modelled in Blender, with baked lighting, running in react-three-fiber. It has GPU rain on the glass, a phone tier, and a plain HTML version for search engines and slow devices.

career.title: Experience and education

experience.summary: Lead developer on full-stack projects for enterprise clients at a creative and dev agency: custom WordPress and React / Next.js sites, end to end. Brought LLM coding agents and custom AI tooling (including a hybrid-search RAG assistant over MCP) into the team, and teaches an internal web development course.
Built and maintained client web apps with React, Node.js / Express and MongoDB. Taught multiple full-stack course cycles of 60–70 students each.
Intensive four-month program of self-led learning and team projects: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, React, Node.js, Express, MongoDB.

stops.label: Laptop · 3D for the web
stops.title: 3D for the web, as a personal project
body: This room is a personal project, not client work. I built it to learn real-time 3D for the web.
It was modelled in Blender with baked lighting, exported as glTF, and runs in react-three-fiber. Phones get a lighter version, and there is a plain HTML page for slow devices.
The laptop screen shows a render of this room.

stops.label: Terrarium · Virtual Garden
stops.title: Virtual Garden
body: The garden grows from your focus. Time on sites you mark as productive grows it, and the rest makes it wilt.

The score is productive ÷ (productive + non-productive). Neutral sites don't count, and it stays at 50 until there are five minutes of data. It's built with WXT and TypeScript, tested with Vitest, and runs CI on every pull request.
